principle: A persistent person or person-equivalent has one continuous identity across development, aging, transformation, retirement and death/end-of-function.
rules: Stage thresholds come from species/entity profiles, not a universal human age table.
Aging changes current biological/visual state while preserving entity identity.

Persistent injuries, augmentations, joining, assimilation, liberation or comparable transformations append history and do not silently replace identity unless a setting rule explicitly defines a new entity.
Death/destruction/end-of-function ends normal active simulation but does not erase identity, history, relationships, records or consequences.
Lifecycle transitions require authoritative events or elapsed-time rules.
Off-screen catch-up may advance lifecycle only through valid dated transitions.
AI cannot declare birth, pregnancy, joining, assimilation, death or revival without authoritative state.
